summary.text: A girl was diagnosed antenatally with a left (ectopic) ureterocele on routine fetal ultrasound at 26 weeks of gestation. She was delivered vaginally at 39 weeks 0 days, 2894 g, with an uneventful perinatal course; two siblings had no urinary tract anomalies.

At one month, postnatal ultrasound showed left hydronephrosis and hydroureter; VCUG showed a ureterocele in the bladder without VUR (VCUG timing differs between sources), and oral amoxicillin 50 mg/day was started as CAP. At three months MRU showed a 33.98 × 26.58 mm ureterocele at the left ureteral orifice and a dilated duplicated renal pelvis (29.83 mm); urine cultures were negative, and TUI-cele was scheduled for eight months.

By six months ultrasound showed ureterocele shrinkage and she was asymptomatic without fever or urinary symptoms; urine culture was negative at seven months. MRU under anesthesia at eight months showed a 21.16 × 10.55 mm ureterocele and an upper-moiety renal pelvis of 13.7 mm, and MAG3 showed DRF 42.6% left and 57.4% right (called preserved). The lower moiety showed no dilatation and no obstruction was found.

Given these results and no febrile UTIs, the planned TUI-cele was cancelled. She had outpatient visits every three months and ultrasound every six months, CAP was discontinued at three years after toilet training, and six-monthly ultrasound and blood tests to eight years confirmed stable ureterocele size, preserved renal morphology and normal renal function.

At eight years the ureterocele was stable, renal function preserved, and she had no urinary symptoms or febrile UTIs; the authors report an infection-free course with surgery avoided even after CAP discontinuation. MRU/MAG3 were not repeated beyond infancy.
